question: After the death of Joshua, which tribe did the LORD appoint to go up first to fight against the Canaanites?
opt1: Judah shall go up: behold, I have delivered the land into his hand
opt2: Ephraim shall go up with their mighty iron chariots
opt3: Dan shall go up with their vanguard archers
opt4: Benjamin shall lead the host before the ark of the covenant
correct: Judah shall go up: behold, I have delivered the land into his hand
explanation: Following Joshua's death, Israel sought divine guidance through the Urim and Thummim, and God appointed the royal tribe of Judah to lead the holy campaign. Judges 1:1-2 (KJV) - "Now after the death of Joshua it came to pass, that the children of Israel asked the LORD, saying, Who shall go up for us against the Canaanites first, to fight against them? And the LORD said, Judah shall go up: behold, I have delivered the land into his hand."

question: Which brother tribe did Judah invite to partner with them in conquering their assigned lot?
opt1: Benjamin his brother, to supply slingers from the mountains
opt2: Simeon his brother, Come up with me into my lot, that we may fight against the Canaanites
opt3: Levi his brother, to carry the sacred vessels before the army
opt4: Reuben the firstborn, to command the cavalry across the plains
correct: Simeon his brother, Come up with me into my lot, that we may fight against the Canaanites
explanation: Judah invited Simeon, whose tribal inheritance lay nested inside Judah's southern border, fostering covenant brotherhood in battle. Judges 1:3 (KJV) - "And Judah said unto Simeon his brother, Come up with me into my lot, that we may fight against the Canaanites; and I likewise will go with thee into thy lot. So Simeon went with him."

question: What mutilation was inflicted upon Adoni-bezek after he was captured in Bezek?
opt1: They put out both his eyes and bound him with fetters of brass
opt2: They branded his forehead with the sign of the tribe of Judah
opt3: They caught him, and cut off his thumbs and his great toes
opt4: They pierced his ears with an awl and made him a bondservant
correct: They caught him, and cut off his thumbs and his great toes
explanation: Cutting off a captured king's thumbs and big toes incapacitated him from wielding a sword or running in battle, rendering him permanently harmless. Judges 1:6 (KJV) - "But Adoni-bezek fled; and they pursued after him, and caught him, and cut off his thumbs and his great toes."

question: How did Adoni-bezek acknowledge God's righteous retribution for his past cruelties?
opt1: I have offered seventy bullocks unto Baal, yet he hath forsaken me in the day of battle
opt2: The gods of the mountains are stronger than the gods of the fertile plains of Canaan
opt3: I have gathered forty talents of gold, which I surrender for the ransom of my life
opt4: Threescore and ten kings, having their thumbs and their great toes cut off, gathered their meat under my table: as I have done, so God hath requited me
correct: Threescore and ten kings, having their thumbs and their great toes cut off, gathered their meat under my table: as I have done, so God hath requited me
explanation: Even a pagan tyrant confessed the inescapable justice of God's lex talionis (the principle of exact retribution): his cruelty to seventy monarchs was visited upon himself. Judges 1:7 (KJV) - "And Adoni-bezek said, Threescore and ten kings, having their thumbs and their great toes cut off, gathered their meat under my table: as I have done, so God hath requited me. And they brought him to Jerusalem, and there he died."

question: What challenge and reward did Caleb proclaim for the capture of Kirjath-sepher?
opt1: He that smiteth Kirjath-sepher, and taketh it, to him will I give Achsah my daughter to wife
opt2: He shall receive fifty shekels of refined silver and a chariot of iron
opt3: He shall be appointed hereditary governor over all the cities of the Negev
opt4: He shall be granted exemption from all future military service in Israel
correct: He that smiteth Kirjath-sepher, and taketh it, to him will I give Achsah my daughter to wife
explanation: Caleb sought a valiant, faith-filled son-in-law worthy of his spiritual heritage, offering his daughter Achsah in marriage to the conqueror of the fortress. Judges 1:12 (KJV) - "And Caleb said, He that smiteth Kirjath-sepher, and taketh it, to him will I give Achsah my daughter to wife."

question: Who captured Kirjath-sepher and received Achsah as his wife?
opt1: Shamgar the son of Anath, the slayer of the Philistines
opt2: Othniel the son of Kenaz, Caleb's younger brother, took it
opt3: Phinehas the son of Eleazar, the zealous priest of Shiloh
opt4: Barak the son of Abinoam, the commander from Kedesh-naphtali
correct: Othniel the son of Kenaz, Caleb's younger brother, took it
explanation: Othniel displayed heroic courage in capturing the citadel, later becoming the very first judge and deliverer of Israel under the power of God's Spirit. Judges 1:13 (KJV) - "And Othniel the son of Kenaz, Caleb's younger brother, took it: and he gave him Achsah his daughter to wife."

question: What gift did Achsah request and receive from her father Caleb when she moved to her new home?
opt1: Give me forty shekels of gold and ten embroidered garments of royal purple
opt2: Give me a troop of fifty horsemen to escort my caravans across the mountains
opt3: Give me a blessing: for thou hast given me a south land; give me also springs of water. And Caleb gave her the upper springs and the nether springs
opt4: Give me a vineyard in the fertile valley of Sorek beside the brook
correct: Give me a blessing: for thou hast given me a south land; give me also springs of water. And Caleb gave her the upper springs and the nether springs
explanation: Achsah wisely recognized that arid southern soil needed living water to flourish; her father generously bestowed both mountain and valley springs. Judges 1:15 (KJV) - "And she said unto him, Give me a blessing: for thou hast given me a south land; give me also springs of water. And Caleb gave her the upper springs and the nether springs."

question: Why could the men of Judah not drive out the inhabitants of the valley, despite conquering the mountain?
opt1: Because their water springs were poisoned by the Amorites
opt2: Because an unseasonal plague decimated the army of Judah
opt3: Because the high priest Eleazar forbade fighting on the Sabbath
opt4: Because they had chariots of iron
correct: Because they had chariots of iron
explanation: Judah's faith faltered before the technologically advanced iron chariots of the Canaanite plains, exposing the tragic beginning of compromise. Judges 1:19 (KJV) - "And the LORD was with Judah; and he drave out the inhabitants of the mountain; but could not drive out the inhabitants of the valley, because they had chariots of iron."

question: Which Kenite clan, related to Moses' father-in-law, went up with Judah to dwell in the south of Arad?
opt1: The children of the Kenite, Moses' father in law, went up out of the city of palm trees with the children of Judah
opt2: The sons of Jethro who returned to the desert of Midian
opt3: The family of Hobab who served as guides in the wilderness of Sin
opt4: The Rechabites who dwelt in tents along the river Jordan
correct: The children of the Kenite, Moses' father in law, went up out of the city of palm trees with the children of Judah
explanation: The Kenites, descendants of Moses' father-in-law Jethro/Reuel, joined Judah in the Negev of Arad, maintaining their peaceful, pastoral nomadic lifestyle in Israel. Judges 1:16 (KJV) - "And the children of the Kenite, Moses' father in law, went up out of the city of palm trees with the children of Judah into the wilderness of Judah, which lieth in the south of Arad; and they went and dwelt among the people."

question: What recurring spiritual failure characterized the northern tribes (Manasseh, Ephraim, Zebulun, Asher, Naphtali) in Judges 1?
opt1: They abandoned the land and migrated back to the fertile delta of Egypt
opt2: Neither did they drive out the Canaanites; but the Canaanites dwelt among them, and became tributaries
opt3: They built wooden fleets and engaged in foreign maritime commerce with Tyre
opt4: They surrendered their cities to the Philistines in exchange for golden idols
correct: Neither did they drive out the Canaanites; but the Canaanites dwelt among them, and became tributaries
explanation: Instead of executing complete obedience to God's command to eradicate Canaanite paganism, the tribes compromised for economic convenience by subjecting the Canaanites to forced tribute. Judges 1:28, 30, 32, 33 (KJV) - "And it came to pass, when Israel was strong, that they put the Canaanites to tribute, and did not utterly drive them out."

question: From where to where did the Angel of the LORD come to deliver a solemn divine rebuke in Judges 2?
opt1: From Mount Sinai unto the sanctuary at Shiloh
opt2: And an angel of the LORD came up from Gilgal to Bochim
opt3: From the river Jordan unto the gates of Jerusalem
opt4: From the cave of Machpelah unto the heights of Bethel
correct: And an angel of the LORD came up from Gilgal to Bochim
explanation: The Angel of the LORD (a pre-incarnate appearance of Christ) moved from Gilgal (place of initial consecration and covenant circumcision) to Bochim ('Weeping') to confront Israel's broken covenant. Judges 2:1 (KJV) - "And an angel of the LORD came up from Gilgal to Bochim, and said, I made you to go up out of Egypt, and have brought you unto the land which I sware unto your fathers; and I said, I will never break my covenant with you."

question: What covenant condition had Israel explicitly violated according to the Angel of the LORD in Judges 2:2?
opt1: Ye have neglected to bring the tithes of wine and corn unto the tabernacle at Shiloh
opt2: Ye have refused to circumcise your male children on the eighth day according to the law
opt3: Ye shall make no league with the inhabitants of this land; ye shall throw down their altars: but ye have not obeyed my voice
opt4: Ye have permitted foreign merchants to sell merchandise inside the holy sanctuary
correct: Ye shall make no league with the inhabitants of this land; ye shall throw down their altars: but ye have not obeyed my voice
explanation: God indicted the nation for unholy compromise: making peaceful political pacts with local pagans and leaving idolatrous altars intact instead of tearing them down. Judges 2:2 (KJV) - "And ye shall make no league with the inhabitants of this land; ye shall throw down their altars: but ye have not obeyed my voice: why have ye done this?"

question: What divine judicial consequence did God pronounce because of Israel's covenant disobedience?
opt1: I will send a consuming fire from heaven to burn your oliveyards and vineyards
opt2: I will cause the waters of the Jordan to flood your encampments forty days
opt3: I will deliver your high priests into the hands of the Pharaoh of Egypt
opt4: I will not drive them out from before you; but they shall be as thorns in your sides, and their gods shall be a snare unto you
correct: I will not drive them out from before you; but they shall be as thorns in your sides, and their gods shall be a snare unto you
explanation: Because Israel refused to drive out the Canaanites, God left them as living instruments of testing and judgment: painful thorns in their sides and perpetual spiritual snares. Judges 2:3 (KJV) - "Wherefore I also said, I will not drive them out from before you; but they shall be as thorns in your sides, and their gods shall be a snare unto you."

question: Why was the name of the place called Bochim?
opt1: Because the people lifted up their voice, and wept, and they sacrificed there unto the LORD
opt2: Because an earthquake split the rocks into deep subterranean fissures
opt3: Because twelve memorial altars of unhewn stone were pitched in a circle
opt4: Because an abundant fountain of sweet water burst forth from the rock
correct: Because the people lifted up their voice, and wept, and they sacrificed there unto the LORD
explanation: 'Bochim' means 'Weepers'; the place was named after the national outpouring of tears and sacrifices when convicted of their spiritual apostasy. Judges 2:4-5 (KJV) - "And it came to pass, when the angel of the LORD spake these words unto all the children of Israel, that the people lifted up their voice, and wept. And they called the name of that place Bochim: and they sacrificed there unto the LORD."

question: How old was Joshua the son of Nun, the servant of the LORD, when he died?
opt1: One hundred and twenty years old, like Moses on Mount Nebo
opt2: An hundred and ten years old (110 years old)
opt3: Eighty-five years old, like Caleb conquering Hebron
opt4: Ninety-nine years old, like Abraham receiving the covenant sign
correct: An hundred and ten years old (110 years old)
explanation: Joshua passed into eternal rest at the age of 110, having faithfully served God as Moses' minister and Israel's victorious military commander. Judges 2:8 (KJV) - "And Joshua the son of Nun, the servant of the LORD, died, being an hundred and ten years old."

question: Where was Joshua buried within his own territorial inheritance?
opt1: In the cave of Machpelah near Hebron beside the patriarchs
opt2: In the sacred sanctuary courtyard at Shiloh before the ark
opt3: In the border of his inheritance in Timnath-heres, in the mount of Ephraim, on the north side of the hill Gaash
opt4: On the mountain peak of Ebal beside the plastered stone altar
correct: In the border of his inheritance in Timnath-heres, in the mount of Ephraim, on the north side of the hill Gaash
explanation: Joshua was laid to rest at Timnath-heres (also called Timnath-serah) in Mount Ephraim, honored for his life of humble servant leadership. Judges 2:9 (KJV) - "And they buried him in the border of his inheritance in Timnath-heres, in the mount of Ephraim, on the north side of the hill Gaash."

question: What tragic spiritual failure occurred after all that generation died and were gathered unto their fathers?
opt1: The twelve tribes divided into separate rival nations and fought a civil war
opt2: The Philistines captured the ark of the covenant and carried it to Ashdod
opt3: The Levites abandoned the tabernacle and ceased offering the daily sacrifice
opt4: There arose another generation after them, which knew not the LORD, nor yet the works which he had done for Israel
correct: There arose another generation after them, which knew not the LORD, nor yet the works which he had done for Israel
explanation: A devastating spiritual breakdown occurred when parents failed to disciple the next generation, producing descendants ignorant of God's miraculous covenant acts. Judges 2:10 (KJV) - "And also all that generation were gathered unto their fathers: and there arose another generation after them, which knew not the LORD, nor yet the works which he had done for Israel."

question: Which specific Canaanite deities did the apostate Israelites serve after forsaking the LORD?
opt1: And they forsook the LORD, and served Baal and Ashtaroth
opt2: Dagon and Chemosh, the gods of the Philistines and Moabites
opt3: Moloch and Remphan, the sun deities of ancient Egypt
opt4: Tammuz and Marduk, the fertility idols of Babylon
correct: And they forsook the LORD, and served Baal and Ashtaroth
explanation: Israel succumbed to the prevailing fertility cults of Canaan: Baal (the storm and fertility god) and Ashtaroth (the goddess of love and warfare). Judges 2:13 (KJV) - "And they forsook the LORD, and served Baal and Ashtaroth."

question: What cyclical pattern of divine grace did the LORD repeatedly display throughout the period of the Judges?
opt1: The LORD anointed kings from the royal tribe of Judah to rule them
opt2: The LORD raised up judges, which delivered them out of the hand of those that spoiled them
opt3: The LORD sent legions of warrior angels with flaming swords to defend their cities
opt4: The LORD scattered them into exile among the empires of the east
correct: The LORD raised up judges, which delivered them out of the hand of those that spoiled them
explanation: The 4-stage cyclical rhythm of Judges (Sin -> Servitude -> Supplication -> Salvation) demonstrated God's relentless mercy in raising up heroic deliverers whenever His people cried out. Judges 2:16 (KJV) - "Nevertheless the LORD raised up judges, which delivered them out of the hand of those that spoiled them."

question: What did the people do as soon as a faithful judge died?
opt1: They observed forty days of national mourning and fasts of repentance
opt2: They gathered at the tabernacle in Shiloh to cast lots for a new prophet
opt3: They returned, and corrupted themselves more than their fathers, in following other gods to serve them
opt4: They built monumental tombs of granite to commemorate the judge's victories
correct: They returned, and corrupted themselves more than their fathers, in following other gods to serve them
explanation: Without inward spiritual regeneration, external leadership brought only temporary outward restraint; upon the judge's death, the nation spiraled into even deeper moral degradation. Judges 2:19 (KJV) - "And it came to pass, when the judge was dead, that they returned, and corrupted themselves more than their fathers, in following other gods to serve them, and to bow down unto them; they ceased not from their own doings, nor from their stubborn way."

question: Why did the LORD leave certain pagan nations in the land of Canaan according to Judges 3:1-2?
opt1: To collect annual tributes of gold and silver to support the tabernacle priests
opt2: Because God lacked the divine power to conquer the walled coastal fortresses
opt3: To prove Israel by them, even as many of Israel as had not known all the wars of Canaan; only that the generations of Israel might know, to teach them war
opt4: To provide domestic bondservants to cultivate the olive orchards and vineyards
correct: To prove Israel by them, even as many of Israel as had not known all the wars of Canaan; only that the generations of Israel might know, to teach them war
explanation: God used the remaining pagan nations as a divine classroom for spiritual and military discipline: testing Israel's covenant obedience and teaching succeeding generations how to wage holy warfare by faith. Judges 3:1-2 (KJV) - "Now these are the nations which the LORD left, to prove Israel by them, even as many of Israel as had not known all the wars of Canaan; Only that the generations of the children of Israel might know, to teach them war, at the least such as before knew nothing thereof;"

question: Who was the Mesopotamian monarch into whose hand God sold Israel for eight years of servitude?
opt1: Eglon king of the Moabite confederacy
opt2: Jabin king of Hazor in northern Canaan
opt3: Hadadezer king of Zobah in Syria
opt4: Chushan-rishathaim king of Mesopotamia
correct: Chushan-rishathaim king of Mesopotamia
explanation: Chushan-rishathaim (meaning 'Chushan of double wickedness') ruled ancient Aram-Naharaim (Mesopotamia), oppressing Israel for eight years until they cried out in repentance. Judges 3:8 (KJV) - "Therefore the anger of the LORD was hot against Israel, and he sold them into the hand of Chushan-rishathaim king of Mesopotamia: and the children of Israel served Chushan-rishathaim eight years."

question: Who was the very first judge raised up by the LORD to deliver Israel from Chushan-rishathaim?
opt1: Othniel the son of Kenaz, Caleb's younger brother
opt2: Ehud the son of Gera the Benjamite
opt3: Shamgar the son of Anath the warrior
opt4: Barak the son of Abinoam of Kedesh
correct: Othniel the son of Kenaz, Caleb's younger brother
explanation: God raised up Caleb's valiant nephew Othniel; empowered by the Holy Spirit, he defeated the Mesopotamian king and brought the land forty years of rest. Judges 3:9-11 (KJV) - "And when the children of Israel cried unto the LORD, the LORD raised up a deliverer to the children of Israel, who delivered them, even Othniel the son of Kenaz, Caleb's younger brother. And the Spirit of the LORD came upon him, and he judged Israel, and went out to war... And the land had rest forty years. And Othniel the son of Kenaz died."

question: Which Moabite king gathered Ammon and Amalek and possessed the city of palm trees (Jericho)?
opt1: Balak the son of Zippor
opt2: Eglon the king of Moab
opt3: Sihon the king of the Amorites
opt4: Mesha the king of the sheepmasters
correct: Eglon the king of Moab
explanation: King Eglon formed a Transjordan coalition, crossed the Jordan, captured the strategic ruins of Jericho ('the city of palm trees'), and oppressed Israel for eighteen years. Judges 3:12-14 (KJV) - "And the children of Israel did evil again in the sight of the LORD: and the LORD strengthened Eglon the king of Moab against Israel... And he gathered unto him the children of Ammon and Amalek, and went and smote Israel, and possessed the city of palm trees. So the children of Israel served Eglon the king of Moab eighteen years."

question: Who was the second judge raised up by God, described as a left-handed Benjamite?
opt1: Elimelech the husband of Naomi
opt2: Abner the son of Ner the commander
opt3: Ehud the son of Gera, a Benjamite, a man lefthanded
opt4: Shimei the son of Gera from Bahurim
correct: Ehud the son of Gera, a Benjamite, a man lefthanded
explanation: Ehud came from the tribe of Benjamin (which ironically means 'son of my right hand'), yet his left-handedness was strategically utilized by God for a covert assassination. Judges 3:15 (KJV) - "But when the children of Israel cried unto the LORD, the LORD raised them up a deliverer, Ehud the son of Gera, a Benjamite, a man lefthanded: and by him the children of Israel sent a present unto Eglon the king of Moab."

question: What unique concealed weapon did Ehud forge to assassinate king Eglon?
opt1: A bronze spear with an iron barb concealed inside a staff
opt2: A poisoned short bow with three silent reed arrows
opt3: A curved scimitar hidden within the royal present of silver
opt4: A dagger which had two edges, of a cubit length; and he did gird it under his raiment upon his right thigh
correct: A dagger which had two edges, of a cubit length; and he did gird it under his raiment upon his right thigh
explanation: Ehud crafted a custom double-edged dagger measuring one cubit (approx. 18 inches) and strapped it to his right thigh, bypassing standard security guards who searched the left side. Judges 3:16 (KJV) - "But Ehud made him a dagger which had two edges, of a cubit length; and he did gird it under his raiment upon his right thigh."

question: What words did Ehud speak to secure a private audience with king Eglon in his summer parlour?
opt1: I have a secret errand unto thee, O king... I have a message from God unto thee
opt2: I bring ten talents of gold from the elders of Mount Ephraim
opt3: A rebellion hath broken out in the camp of the Philistines
opt4: The stars have revealed a vision of perpetual victory for Moab
correct: I have a secret errand unto thee, O king... I have a message from God unto thee
explanation: Ehud's declaration ('I have a message from God unto thee') caused the obese king to stand up in reverence, allowing Ehud to strike the fatal blow. Judges 3:19-20 (KJV) - "...I have a secret errand unto thee, O king: who said, Keep silence. And all that stood by him went out from him. And Ehud came unto him; and he was sitting in a summer parlour, which he had for himself alone. And Ehud said, I have a message from God unto thee. And he arose out of his seat."

question: What physical detail is recorded concerning the death of Eglon when Ehud thrust the dagger into his belly?
opt1: The king cried aloud with a great shout that alarmed all the palace guards
opt2: And the haft also went in after the blade; and the fat closed upon the blade, so that he could not draw the dagger out of his belly
opt3: The blade shattered against the king's hidden breastplate of iron
opt4: The dagger severed the golden chain suspended around the monarch's neck
correct: And the haft also went in after the blade; and the fat closed upon the blade, so that he could not draw the dagger out of his belly
explanation: Because Eglon was exceedingly fat, the entire dagger, handle and all, sank completely into his abdomen, and Ehud calmly locked the doors of the parlour and escaped. Judges 3:21-23 (KJV) - "And Ehud put forth his left hand, and took the dagger from his right thigh, and thrust it into his belly: And the haft also went in after the blade; and the fat closed upon the blade, so that he could not draw the dagger out of his belly... Then Ehud went forth through the porch, and shut the doors of the parlour upon him, and locked them."

question: How many Moabite warriors were slain when Ehud blew the trumpet in Mount Ephraim and seized the fords of Jordan?
opt1: Five thousand archers and fifty royal charioteers
opt2: Twenty thousand soldiers carrying bronze shields
opt3: About ten thousand men, all lusty, and all men of valour; and there escaped not a man
opt4: One hundred thousand footmen of the Moabite host
correct: About ten thousand men, all lusty, and all men of valour; and there escaped not a man
explanation: Israel seized the shallow fords of Jordan, cutting off the Moabite army's retreat and wiping out ten thousand elite enemy soldiers, bringing eighty years of rest. Judges 3:28-30 (KJV) - "And they slew of Moab at that time about ten thousand men, all lusty, and all men of valour; and there escaped not a man. So Moab was subdued that day under the hand of Israel. And the land had rest fourscore years."

question: Who was the third judge, and with what rustic weapon did he deliver Israel by slaying 600 Philistines?
opt1: Jair the Gileadite, who used thirty bronze battle axes
opt2: Tola the son of Puah, who fought with an iron broadsword
opt3: Ibzan of Bethlehem, who commanded three hundred bowmen
opt4: Shamgar the son of Anath, which slew of the Philistines six hundred men with an ox goad: and he also delivered Israel
correct: Shamgar the son of Anath, which slew of the Philistines six hundred men with an ox goad: and he also delivered Israel
explanation: God can achieve extraordinary deliverance using humble, ordinary instruments: Shamgar routed six hundred Philistines using only a long agricultural ox goad. Judges 3:31 (KJV) - "And after him was Shamgar the son of Anath, which slew of the Philistines six hundred men with an ox goad: and he also delivered Israel."

question: Which northern Canaanite king oppressed Israel for twenty years following the death of Ehud?
opt1: Adoni-zedek the ruler of Jerusalem
opt2: Og the giant monarch of Bashan
opt3: Sihon the Amorite sovereign of Heshbon
opt4: Jabin king of Canaan, that reigned in Hazor
correct: Jabin king of Canaan, that reigned in Hazor
explanation: A rebuilt Hazor under a second King Jabin oppressed northern Israel severely for two decades with formidable military technology. Judges 4:2-3 (KJV) - "And the LORD sold them into the hand of Jabin king of Canaan, that reigned in Hazor; the captain of whose host was Sisera, which dwelt in Harosheth of the Gentiles. And the children of Israel cried unto the LORD: for he had nine hundred chariots of iron; and twenty years he mightily oppressed the children of Israel."

question: Who was the commander of Jabin's formidable army, and how many iron chariots did he command?
opt1: Sisera, who had nine hundred chariots of iron
opt2: Piram, who had five hundred bronze war wagons
opt3: Jobab, who commanded seven hundred cavalry units
opt4: Hoham, who had three hundred iron battering rams
correct: Sisera, who had nine hundred chariots of iron
explanation: Sisera based his iron chariot corps at Harosheth of the Gentiles, terrorizing the valley roads and trade routes of northern Israel. Judges 4:2-3 (KJV).

question: Who judged Israel at that time under a palm tree between Ramah and Bethel in Mount Ephraim?
opt1: Huldah the prophetess, the wife of Shallum
opt2: Deborah, a prophetess, the wife of Lapidoth, she judged Israel at that time
opt3: Miriam the prophetess, the sister of Aaron
opt4: Anna the prophetess, the daughter of Phanuel
correct: Deborah, a prophetess, the wife of Lapidoth, she judged Israel at that time
explanation: Deborah served as a spiritual prophetess, judge, and national counselor, holding court under the 'Palm Tree of Deborah' in Mount Ephraim. Judges 4:4-5 (KJV) - "And Deborah, a prophetess, the wife of Lapidoth, she judged Israel at that time. And she dwelt under the palm tree of Deborah between Ramah and Bethel in mount Ephraim: and the children of Israel came up to her for judgment."

question: Whom did Deborah summon from Kedesh-naphtali to lead ten thousand men against Sisera?
opt1: Gideon the son of Joash from Ophrah
opt2: Jephthah the Gileadite from the land of Tob
opt3: Barak the son of Abinoam out of Kedesh-naphtali
opt4: Samson the son of Manoah from Zorah
correct: Barak the son of Abinoam out of Kedesh-naphtali
explanation: Acting under divine command, Deborah appointed Barak to mobilize ten thousand warriors from Naphtali and Zebulun to confront Sisera at Mount Tabor. Judges 4:6 (KJV) - "And she sent and called Barak the son of Abinoam out of Kedesh-naphtali, and said unto him, Hath not the LORD God of Israel commanded, saying, Go and draw toward mount Tabor, and take with thee ten thousand men of the children of Naphtali and of the children of Zebulun?"

question: Under what condition did Barak agree to march into battle against Sisera's iron chariots?
opt1: If the high priest bringeth the ark of the covenant from Shiloh to lead the vanguard
opt2: If the tribe of Judah sendeth forty thousand archers to support our flank
opt3: If the elders of Gilead provide two thousand horses for our cavalry
opt4: If thou wilt go with me, then I will go: but if thou wilt not go with me, then I will not go
correct: If thou wilt go with me, then I will go: but if thou wilt not go with me, then I will not go
explanation: Recognizing Deborah as the prophetic voice of God's presence, Barak refused to march unless she personally accompanied the army to the battlefield. Judges 4:8 (KJV) - "And Barak said unto her, If thou wilt go with me, then I will go: but if thou wilt not go with me, then I will not go."

question: What prophetic consequence did Deborah declare regarding the honour of the victory because of Barak's hesitation?
opt1: The journey that thou takest shall not be for thine honour; for the LORD shall sell Sisera into the hand of a woman
opt2: Barak shall fall by the sword of a Canaanite archer before the gates of Hazor
opt3: The ten thousand men shall be taken captive and carried unto Harosheth
opt4: The kingdom of Hazor shall extract an annual tribute of silver from Naphtali
correct: The journey that thou takest shall not be for thine honour; for the LORD shall sell Sisera into the hand of a woman
explanation: Deborah prophesied that the supreme military glory of capturing or slaying the enemy commander would not belong to general Barak, but to a woman. Judges 4:9 (KJV) - "And she said, I will surely go with thee: notwithstanding the journey that thou takest shall not be for thine honour; for the LORD shall sell Sisera into the hand of a woman. And Deborah arose, and went with Barak to Kedesh."

question: Near which ancient river did the battle between Barak and Sisera take place?
opt1: The river Jordan near the fords of Jericho
opt2: The river Kishon, where the LORD discomfited Sisera and all his chariots
opt3: The river Jabbok bordering the Ammonites
opt4: The river Arnon bordering the Moabites
correct: The river Kishon, where the LORD discomfited Sisera and all his chariots
explanation: God used a supernatural cloudburst and flood along the Kishon River to turn the valley into a muddy mire, rendering Sisera's 900 iron chariots completely useless. Judges 4:7, 15 (KJV) - "And I will draw unto thee to the river Kishon Sisera, the captain of Jabin's army, with his chariots and his multitude; and I will deliver him into thine hand... And the LORD discomfited Sisera, and all his chariots, and all his host, with the edge of the sword before Barak; so that Sisera lighted down off his chariot, and fled away on his feet."

question: To whose tent did the defeated Sisera flee on foot seeking sanctuary?
opt1: To the palace of the king of Megiddo in the valley
opt2: To the fortress of Harosheth of the Gentiles in the north
opt3: To the tent of Jael the wife of Heber the Kenite: for there was peace between Jabin the king of Hazor and the house of Heber
opt4: To the sanctuary of Baal in the city of Shechem
correct: To the tent of Jael the wife of Heber the Kenite: for there was peace between Jabin the king of Hazor and the house of Heber
explanation: Sisera sought refuge with the neutral Kenites, entering Jael's tent because ancient nomad hospitality strictly forbade entering a woman's quarters, making it an ideal hiding place. Judges 4:17 (KJV) - "Howbeit Sisera fled away on his feet to the tent of Jael the wife of Heber the Kenite: for there was peace between Jabin the king of Hazor and the house of Heber the Kenite."

question: What refreshing beverage did Jael give unto Sisera when he asked for water to drink?
opt1: She brought wine in a golden goblet from Harosheth
opt2: She gave him cold water drawn from the spring of Kishon
opt3: She served pomegranate juice mixed with honey and spices
opt4: She opened a bottle of milk, and gave him drink, and covered him
correct: She opened a bottle of milk, and gave him drink, and covered him
explanation: Jael served him thick curdled milk (laban), which not only quenched his thirst but induced deep physical exhaustion and slumber. Judges 4:19 (KJV) - "And he said unto her, Give me, I pray thee, a little water to drink; for I am thirsty. And she opened a bottle of milk, and gave him drink, and covered him."

question: With what household implements did Jael execute the sleeping commander Sisera?
opt1: A nail of the tent (tent peg) and an hammer in her hand, and smote the nail into his temples, and fastened it into the ground
opt2: Sisera's own two-edged bronze broadsword while he lay asleep
opt3: A hunting spear of polished acacia wood tipped with iron
opt4: A heavy grinding millstone dropped from the tent post
correct: A nail of the tent (tent peg) and an hammer in her hand, and smote the nail into his temples, and fastened it into the ground
explanation: Fulfilling Deborah's prophecy, Jael used everyday nomadic tools—a wooden tent peg and mallet—to drive the stake through Sisera's temples into the earth. Judges 4:21 (KJV) - "Then Jael Heber's wife took a nail of the tent, and took an hammer in her hand, and went softly unto him, and smote the nail into his temples, and fastened it into the ground: for he was fast asleep and weary. So he died."

question: What literary and musical masterpiece was sung by Deborah and Barak on the day of victory?
opt1: The Song of Deborah and Barak, one of the oldest and most magnificent poetic victory odes in the Bible
opt2: The Psalm of Asaph commemorating the destruction of the Canaanites
opt3: The Lamentation of the Daughters of Shiloh beside the river Kishon
opt4: The Proverb of the Ten Thousand Princes of Naphtali and Zebulun
correct: The Song of Deborah and Barak, one of the oldest and most magnificent poetic victory odes in the Bible
explanation: Judges 5 contains an ancient, inspired triumphal victory ode celebrating God's majesty, the heroism of faithful tribes, and the overthrow of Canaan's oppressors. Judges 5:1-2 (KJV) - "Then sang Deborah and Barak the son of Abinoam on that day, saying, Praise ye the LORD for the avenging of Israel, when the people willingly offered themselves."

question: How does the Song describe the dangerous condition of the highways before Deborah arose as a mother in Israel?
opt1: The roads were crowded with Roman garrisons collecting heavy taxes
opt2: The highways were unoccupied, and the travellers walked through byways... until that I Deborah arose, that I arose a mother in Israel
opt3: The highways were submerged under perpetual floodwaters from Jordan
opt4: The travelers paid fifty shekels of silver at every gate of the cities
correct: The highways were unoccupied, and the travellers walked through byways... until that I Deborah arose, that I arose a mother in Israel
explanation: Due to Canaanite raiding parties, commerce and travel had ceased on main roads, forcing citizens to sneak through hidden backcountry trails until Deborah's spiritual leadership restored peace. Judges 5:6-7 (KJV) - "In the days of Shamgar the son of Anath, in the days of Jael, the highways were unoccupied, and the travellers walked through byways. The inhabitants of the villages ceased, they ceased in Israel, until that I Deborah arose, that I arose a mother in Israel."

question: What disarmament condition of Israel was lamented before God gave them victory in Judges 5:8?
opt1: There were no horses or chariots left in the stables of Ephraim
opt2: The iron smelters of Dan had been confiscated by the Philistines
opt3: Was there a shield or spear seen among forty thousand in Israel?
opt4: The archers of Benjamin had depleted all their arrows in the wilderness
correct: Was there a shield or spear seen among forty thousand in Israel?
explanation: The oppressing Canaanites had systematically disarmed Israel, leaving forty thousand men without standard shields or spears, magnifying the supernatural nature of God's victory. Judges 5:8 (KJV) - "They chose new gods; then was war in the gates: was there a shield or spear seen among forty thousand in Israel?"

question: Which four tribes were rebuked in the Song of Deborah for their selfish indifference and refusal to join the battle?
opt1: Judah, Benjamin, Simeon, and the house of Levi in the south
opt2: Ephraim, Manasseh, Issachar, and the children of Naphtali
opt3: The priests of Shiloh, the elders of Bethel, and the judges of Gilgal
opt4: Reuben (great thoughts of heart), Gilead/Gad (abode beyond Jordan), Dan (remained in ships), and Asher (abode on the breach)
correct: Reuben (great thoughts of heart), Gilead/Gad (abode beyond Jordan), Dan (remained in ships), and Asher (abode on the breach)
explanation: Deborah boldly exposed tribal apathy: Reuben debated endlessly by sheepfolds, Gilead stayed east of Jordan, Dan tended ships, and Asher lingered on beaches instead of helping their brethren. Judges 5:15-17 (KJV).

question: Which two tribes were singled out for glorious praise for hazarding their lives unto death in the high places of the field?
opt1: Zebulun and Naphtali were a people that jeoparded their lives unto the death in the high places of the field
opt2: Judah and Benjamin who provided forty thousand seasoned cavalry
opt3: Dan and Asher who launched an armed naval assault against Tyre
opt4: Reuben and Gad who marched across the swollen torrents of Jordan
correct: Zebulun and Naphtali were a people that jeoparded their lives unto the death in the high places of the field
explanation: Zebulun and Naphtali demonstrated sacrificial, heroic faith, charging straight down Mount Tabor against 900 iron chariots and risking everything for God's cause. Judges 5:18 (KJV) - "Zebulun and Naphtali were a people that jeoparded their lives unto the death in the high places of the field."

question: What cosmic and elemental allies fought against Sisera according to Judges 5:20-21?
opt1: A plague of biting hornets drove their war horses into the mountain caves
opt2: They fought from heaven; the stars in their courses fought against Sisera. The river of Kishon swept them away
opt3: A pillar of consuming fire fell from heaven upon their wooden camp
opt4: An earthquake swallowed the entire city of Harosheth of the Gentiles
correct: They fought from heaven; the stars in their courses fought against Sisera. The river of Kishon swept them away
explanation: Creation itself aligned with God's purpose: torrential rains (astronomically described as 'the stars in their courses') transformed the dry Kishon into a raging torrent that drowned Sisera's army. Judges 5:20-21 (KJV) - "They fought from heaven; the stars in their courses fought against Sisera. The river of Kishon swept them away, that ancient river, the river Kishon. O my soul, thou hast trodden down strength."

question: What village or city was severely cursed by the Angel of the LORD for failing to come to the help of the LORD against the mighty?
opt1: Curse ye Jericho, because its gates were barred against the priests
opt2: Curse ye Bethel, because its shrines were dedicated to golden calves
opt3: Curse ye Meroz, said the angel of the LORD, curse ye bitterly the inhabitants thereof; because they came not to the help of the LORD
opt4: Curse ye Megiddo, because its merchants traded with Canaanite kings
correct: Curse ye Meroz, said the angel of the LORD, curse ye bitterly the inhabitants thereof; because they came not to the help of the LORD
explanation: Meroz was strategically located near the battlefield, but its citizens cowardly stood by doing nothing; their sin of passive neutral disobedience earned a bitter divine curse. Judges 5:23 (KJV) - "Curse ye Meroz, said the angel of the LORD, curse ye bitterly the inhabitants thereof; because they came not to the help of the LORD, to the help of the LORD against the mighty."

question: What exalted blessing was pronounced upon Jael the wife of Heber the Kenite in Judges 5:24?
opt1: She shall receive an eternal portion in the royal kingdom of David
opt2: Her daughters shall be appointed high priestesses before the tabernacle
opt3: Her sons shall govern the forty-eight cities of the Levites in peace
opt4: Blessed above women shall Jael the wife of Heber the Kenite be, blessed shall she be above women in the tent
correct: Blessed above women shall Jael the wife of Heber the Kenite be, blessed shall she be above women in the tent
explanation: Jael was celebrated for her bold initiative in crushing the head of the oppressor, foreshadowing Mary through whom the ultimate Serpent-Crusher would be born (Gen 3:15, Luke 1:42). Judges 5:24 (KJV) - "Blessed above women shall Jael the wife of Heber the Kenite be, blessed shall she be above women in the tent."

question: What dramatic scene does the Song depict concerning Sisera's mother waiting for his return?
opt1: The mother of Sisera looked out at a window, and cried through the lattice, Why is his chariot so long in coming? why tarry the wheels of his chariots?
opt2: She offered seven white heifers upon the golden altars of Hazor
opt3: She commanded fifty royal maidens to weave a crown of laurels for his brow
opt4: She sent runners across the plain carrying twenty talents of ransom gold
correct: The mother of Sisera looked out at a window, and cried through the lattice, Why is his chariot so long in coming? why tarry the wheels of his chariots?
explanation: In poignant dramatic irony, the poem contrasts Sisera's mother anticipating her son returning with plundered spoils and maiden captives, unaware that he lay dead with a tent peg through his skull. Judges 5:28 (KJV) - "The mother of Sisera looked out at a window, and cried through the lattice, Why is his chariot so long in coming? why tarry the wheels of his chariots?"

question: What triumphant prayer and duration of peace concludes the Song of Deborah in Judges 5:31?
opt1: Establish thy throne in Jerusalem forever, and give Israel rest for seventy years
opt2: So let all thine enemies perish, O LORD: but let them that love him be as the sun when he goeth forth in his might. And the land had rest forty years
opt3: Send thy angels to guard the fords of Jordan, and grant peace for twenty years
opt4: Anoint Barak as king over the twelve tribes, and let the land rest fifty years
correct: So let all thine enemies perish, O LORD: but let them that love him be as the sun when he goeth forth in his might. And the land had rest forty years
explanation: The song concludes with an inspiring doxological prayer that all God's enemies perish while those who love Him shine like the radiant midday sun, ushering in forty years of peace. Judges 5:31 (KJV) - "So let all thine enemies perish, O LORD: but let them that love him be as the sun when he goeth forth in his might. And the land had rest forty years."

question: Which nomadic invaders oppressed Israel for seven years, destroying the increase of the earth like grasshoppers?
opt1: The Philistine lords of the five southwestern maritime cities
opt2: The Midianites, and the Amalekites, and the children of the east
opt3: The legions of the Pharaoh of Egypt marching from the delta
opt4: The Syrian armies of Damascus armed with iron spears
correct: The Midianites, and the Amalekites, and the children of the east
explanation: Midian, allied with Amalek and desert nomads, invaded Israel during harvest like swarming locusts ('grasshoppers for multitude'), forcing Israelites into mountain dens, caves, and strongholds. Judges 6:3-5 (KJV) - "And so it was, when Israel had sown, that the Midianites came up, and the Amalekites, and the children of the east, even they came up against them... and destroyed the increase of the earth... for they came as grasshoppers for multitude; for both they and their camels were without number: and they entered into the land to destroy it."

question: What was Gideon the son of Joash doing when the Angel of the LORD appeared unto him in Ophrah?
opt1: Offering a young bullock upon the stone altar of the town gate
opt2: Polishing his bronze broadsword within the family tent
opt3: Threshing wheat by the winepress, to hide it from the Midianites
opt4: Consulting the elders of Manasseh concerning a military alliance
correct: Threshing wheat by the winepress, to hide it from the Midianites
explanation: Wheat was normally threshed in elevated, open, windy threshing floors, but fear of Midianite raiders compelled Gideon to beat out grain secretly in a sunken, hidden winepress. Judges 6:11 (KJV) - "And there came an angel of the LORD, and sat under an oak which was in Ophrah, that pertained unto Joash the Abi-ezrite: and his son Gideon threshed wheat by the winepress, to hide it from the Midianites."

question: What surprising greeting did the Angel of the LORD proclaim unto the fearful Gideon?
opt1: Arise, O prince of Manasseh, and take the crown of Israel
opt2: Why hidest thou like a fearful child in the dark winepress?
opt3: Prepare forty talents of silver to purchase peace from Midian
opt4: The LORD is with thee, thou mighty man of valour
correct: The LORD is with thee, thou mighty man of valour
explanation: God looks not at present outward circumstances or human timidity, but calls things that be not as though they were, declaring Gideon a 'mighty man of valour' through divine empowerment. Judges 6:12 (KJV) - "And the angel of the LORD appeared unto him, and said unto him, The LORD is with thee, thou mighty man of valour."

question: What honest, searching question did Gideon ask in response to the Angel's greeting?
opt1: Oh my Lord, if the LORD be with us, why then is all this befallen us? and where be all his miracles which our fathers told us of?
opt2: How shall one thousand poor farmers overcome ninety thousand iron chariots?
opt3: Art thou an ambassador from the kings of Egypt sent with military legions?
opt4: When wilt thou deliver the sacred vessels of the tabernacle from the enemy?
correct: Oh my Lord, if the LORD be with us, why then is all this befallen us? and where be all his miracles which our fathers told us of?
explanation: Gideon voiced the deep perplexity of suffering believers, questioning why, if God was with them, they were experiencing crushing oppression and the absence of historical miracles. Judges 6:13 (KJV) - "And Gideon said unto him, Oh my Lord, if the LORD be with us, why then is all this befallen us? and where be all his miracles which our fathers told us of, saying, Did not the LORD bring us up from Egypt? but now the LORD hath forsaken us, and delivered us into the hands of the Midianites."

question: What divine commission and assurance did the LORD give to Gideon in Judges 6:14?
opt1: Gather forty thousand archers from Judah and lay siege to Harosheth
opt2: Go in this thy might, and thou shalt save Israel from the hand of the Midianites: have not I sent thee?
opt3: Take the gold plundered from Jericho and build a fortress on Mount Tabor
opt4: Wait until forty years of captivity have elapsed according to prophecy
correct: Go in this thy might, and thou shalt save Israel from the hand of the Midianites: have not I sent thee?
explanation: Gideon's true might was not in human armaments, but in the divine commission: 'Have not I sent thee? Surely I will be with thee.' Judges 6:14, 16 (KJV) - "And the LORD looked upon him, and said, Go in this thy might, and thou shalt save Israel from the hand of the Midianites: have not I sent thee?... Surely I will be with thee, and thou shalt smite the Midianites as one man."

question: What supernatural sign consumed Gideon's offering of kid's flesh and unleavened cakes upon the rock?
opt1: Lightning flashed from a clear noon sky and struck the stone altar
opt2: The rock opened and swallowed the kid into subterranean waters
opt3: The angel of the LORD put forth the end of the staff that was in his hand, and touched the flesh and the unleavened cakes; and there rose up fire out of the rock, and consumed them
opt4: The offering dissolved into a pillar of sweet fragrant incense cloud
correct: The angel of the LORD put forth the end of the staff that was in his hand, and touched the flesh and the unleavened cakes; and there rose up fire out of the rock, and consumed them
explanation: When the divine Messenger touched the sacrifice with the tip of His staff, miraculous fire erupted directly from the stone rock, confirming the divine presence. Judges 6:21 (KJV) - "Then the angel of the LORD put forth the end of the staff that was in his hand, and touched the flesh and the unleavened cakes; and there rose up fire out of the rock, and consumed the flesh and the unleavened cakes. Then the angel of the LORD departed out of his sight."

question: What name did Gideon give to the altar he built in Ophrah after God reassured him, 'Peace be unto thee; fear not'?
opt1: Jehovah-jireh (The LORD will provide)
opt2: Jehovah-nissi (The LORD our banner)
opt3: Jehovah-tsidkenu (The LORD our righteousness)
opt4: Jehovah-shalom (The LORD send peace)
correct: Jehovah-shalom (The LORD send peace)
explanation: Terrified that he would die after seeing the Angel of God face to face, Gideon received divine peace and commemorated it by building the altar 'Jehovah-shalom' ('The LORD is Peace'). Judges 6:24 (KJV) - "Then Gideon built an altar there unto the LORD, and called it Jehovah-shalom: unto this day it is yet in Ophrah of the Abi-ezrites."

question: What radical act of obedience was Gideon commanded to perform by night against local idolatry?
opt1: Throw down the altar of Baal that thy father hath, and cut down the grove that is by it, and build an altar unto the LORD thy God upon the top of this rock
opt2: Banish the priests of Baal into the eastern wilderness of Ammon
opt3: Burn the grain storage barns of the Midianites along the plain
opt4: Smite the high places of Chemosh on the mountains of Moab
correct: Throw down the altar of Baal that thy father hath, and cut down the grove that is by it, and build an altar unto the LORD thy God upon the top of this rock
explanation: Before God could deliver Israel from external oppressors, internal family and national idolatry had to be purged: Gideon tore down his father's Baal altar and cut down the pagan Asherah grove. Judges 6:25-27 (KJV).

question: How did Gideon's father Joash defend his son against the angry townspeople who demanded his execution?
opt1: My son hath acted under the military authority of the high priest of Shiloh
opt2: Will ye plead for Baal? will ye save him? if he be a god, let him plead for himself, because one hath cast down his altar
opt3: I will pay one hundred shekels of silver for each broken stone of the altar
opt4: Let the seventy elders cast lots to decide whether Gideon should die
correct: Will ye plead for Baal? will ye save him? if he be a god, let him plead for himself, because one hath cast down his altar
explanation: Joash exposed the impotence of idolatry: if Baal were truly a god, he should be able to avenge himself rather than requiring mortal men to defend him; hence Gideon was named 'Jerubbaal' ('Let Baal plead'). Judges 6:31-32 (KJV) - "And Joash said unto all that stood against him, Will ye plead for Baal? will ye save him?... if he be a god, let him plead for himself, because one hath cast down his altar. Therefore on that day he called him Jerubbaal, saying, Let Baal plead against him..."

question: What two fleece tests did Gideon put before God to confirm that God would save Israel by his hand?
opt1: First, the fleece turned pure white; second, the fleece turned deep royal purple
opt2: First, fire descended upon the fleece; second, water gushed from beneath the wool
opt3: First, dew on the fleece only while the earth remained dry; second, dry on the fleece only while dew covered all the ground
opt4: First, the fleece floated in the air; second, the fleece doubled its weight in silver
correct: First, dew on the fleece only while the earth remained dry; second, dry on the fleece only while dew covered all the ground
explanation: In patient condescension to Gideon's struggling faith, God miraculously granted two opposite signs on consecutive nights—first wetting only the fleece (wringing out a bowlful of water), then wetting only the surrounding earth. Judges 6:36-40 (KJV).

question: Why did the LORD instruct Gideon to reduce his initial army of thirty-two thousand men?
opt1: Because there was an insufficient supply of barley bread to feed the host
opt2: Because the narrow pass between the mountains could accommodate only three hundred soldiers
opt3: The people that are with thee are too many for me to give the Midianites into their hands, lest Israel vaunt themselves against me, saying, Mine own hand hath saved me
opt4: Because Moses had commanded that no Hebrew army should exceed ten thousand men
correct: The people that are with thee are too many for me to give the Midianites into their hands, lest Israel vaunt themselves against me, saying, Mine own hand hath saved me
explanation: God will not share His glory with human flesh: a massive army would tempt Israel to boast in their own prowess rather than attributing total salvation to God alone. Judges 7:2 (KJV) - "And the LORD said unto Gideon, The people that are with thee are too many for me to give the Midianites into their hands, lest Israel vaunt themselves against me, saying, Mine own hand hath saved me."

question: What proclamation in accordance with Deuteronomy 20:8 resulted in twenty-two thousand men leaving the army?
opt1: Whosoever hath not trained with the iron broadsword, let him return home
opt2: Whosoever hath married a wife within the year, let him depart to his farm
opt3: Whosoever hath planted a vineyard and not eaten of it, let him turn back
opt4: Whosoever is fearful and afraid, let him return and depart early from mount Gilead
correct: Whosoever is fearful and afraid, let him return and depart early from mount Gilead
explanation: Fear is contagious in spiritual warfare; when Gideon dismissed the faint-hearted, over two-thirds (22,000 out of 32,000) immediately abandoned the campaign. Judges 7:3 (KJV) - "Now therefore go to, proclaim in the ears of the people, saying, Whosoever is fearful and afraid, let him return and depart early from mount Gilead. And there returned of the people twenty and two thousand; and there remained ten thousand."

question: By what water-drinking test at the brook did the LORD separate the final elite company of three hundred men?
opt1: Every one that lappeth of the water with his tongue, as a dog lappeth (putting hand to mouth)... three hundred men: but all the rest of the people bowed down upon their knees to drink water
opt2: Those who drank while swimming across the current versus those who stood on the bank
opt3: Those who drank from their bronze helmets versus those who drank directly from the stream
opt4: Those who drank after offering a prayer versus those who drank without blessing God
correct: Every one that lappeth of the water with his tongue, as a dog lappeth (putting hand to mouth)... three hundred men: but all the rest of the people bowed down upon their knees to drink water
explanation: The three hundred men who lapped water by scooping it to their mouths remained alert, watchful, and combat-ready, while the others knelt carelessly with faces buried in the water. Judges 7:5-7 (KJV) - "And the number of them that lapped, putting their hand to their mouth, were three hundred men: but all the rest of the people bowed down upon their knees to drink water. And the LORD said unto Gideon, By the three hundred men that lapped will I save you, and deliver the Midianites into thine hand..."

question: What dream did Gideon overhear a Midianite soldier telling his companion in the valley at midnight?
opt1: A mighty golden eagle descended from heaven and carried away our royal battle standards
opt2: Behold, I dreamed a dream, and, lo, a cake of barley bread tumbled into the host of Midian, and came unto a tent, and smote it that it fell, and overturned it
opt3: A sudden river of water flooded the dry valley and drowned forty thousand of our camels
opt4: Three hundred lions with burning torches leaped into our camp and devoured our generals
correct: Behold, I dreamed a dream, and, lo, a cake of barley bread tumbled into the host of Midian, and came unto a tent, and smote it that it fell, and overturned it
explanation: God used a humble, rustic symbol—a coarse barley cake (representing peasant agricultural Israel)—tumbling down the hill and smashing the luxurious nomad tent of Midian to signify total defeat. Judges 7:13 (KJV) - "And when Gideon was come, behold, there was a man that told a dream unto his fellow, and said, Behold, I dreamed a dream, and, lo, a cake of barley bread tumbled into the host of Midian, and came unto a tent, and smote it that it fell, and overturned it, that the tent lay along."

question: How did the Midianite soldier's comrade interpret the dream of the tumbling barley cake?
opt1: This signifieth that a severe winter famine shall destroy our livestock in the spring
opt2: This portendeth that the kings of Egypt are marching to demand tribute of our plunder
opt3: This is nothing else save the sword of Gideon the son of Joash, a man of Israel: for into his hand hath God delivered Midian, and all the host
opt4: This is merely a night terror born of excessive drinking of wine at the feast
correct: This is nothing else save the sword of Gideon the son of Joash, a man of Israel: for into his hand hath God delivered Midian, and all the host
explanation: God had already planted deep psychological terror and conviction of doom inside the enemy's heart, providing Gideon with absolute supernatural confirmation before the attack. Judges 7:14 (KJV) - "And his fellow answered and said, This is nothing else save the sword of Gideon the son of Joash, a man of Israel: for into his hand hath God delivered Midian, and all the host."

question: Into how many companies did Gideon divide his three hundred men, and what unconventional weapons did he place in their hands?
opt1: Two companies armed with long bronze spears and heavy round shields
opt2: Four companies equipped with short bows and flaming sulphur arrows
opt3: Ten companies carrying iron battle axes and ropes of camel hair
opt4: Three companies; and he put a trumpet in every man's hand, with empty pitchers, and lamps within the pitchers
correct: Three companies; and he put a trumpet in every man's hand, with empty pitchers, and lamps within the pitchers
explanation: Gideon's men held no conventional swords in their hands: each carried a ram's horn trumpet in one hand and an earthenware pitcher concealing a burning torch in the other. Judges 7:16 (KJV) - "And he divided the three hundred men into three companies, and he put a trumpet in every man's hand, with empty pitchers, and lamps within the pitchers."

question: What rallying battle cry did Gideon command his three companies to shout as they broke their pitchers?
opt1: The sword of the LORD, and of Gideon!
opt2: Victory for the house of Joseph and the tribes of Galilee!
opt3: Arise, O God, and let thine enemies be scattered in the desert!
opt4: Down with the altars of Baal and the groves of the Amorites!
correct: The sword of the LORD, and of Gideon!
explanation: At midnight, surrounding the sleeping camp on three sides, the sudden blare of 300 trumpets, crashing pottery, blazing torches, and the thunderous cry 'The sword of the LORD, and of Gideon!' shattered the night. Judges 7:18, 20 (KJV) - "...Then blow ye the trumpets also on every side of all the camp, and say, The sword of the LORD, and of Gideon... And they cried, The sword of the LORD, and of Gideon."

question: What supernatural chaos occurred within the Midianite camp when the three hundred trumpets sounded?
opt1: A sudden earthquake swallowed the tents of the kings of Midian
opt2: All the host ran, and cried, and fled. And the LORD set every man's sword against his fellow, even throughout all the host
opt3: Heavy hailstones from heaven fell and destroyed their cavalry
opt4: The river Kishon overflowed its banks and swept away their encampment
correct: All the host ran, and cried, and fled. And the LORD set every man's sword against his fellow, even throughout all the host

Judges 7:21-22 (KJV) - "And they stood every man in his place round about the camp; and all the host ran, and cried, and fled. And the three hundred blew the trumpets, and the LORD set every man's sword against his fellow, even throughout all the host..."

question: Which tribe did Gideon summon to seize the waters of the Jordan to cut off the fleeing Midianites?
opt1: The men of Judah from the southern hill country

opt3: The men of Ephraim gathered themselves together, and took the waters unto Beth-barah and Jordan
opt4: The horsemen of Gad from the forests of Gilead
correct: The men of Ephraim gathered themselves together, and took the waters unto Beth-barah and Jordan
explanation: Gideon dispatched messengers throughout Mount Ephraim to secure the Jordan river crossings, trapping the routed Midianites as they fled eastward. Judges 7:24 (KJV) - "And Gideon sent messengers throughout all mount Ephraim, saying, Come down against the Midianites, and take before them the waters unto Beth-barah and Jordan. Then all the men of Ephraim gathered themselves together, and took the waters unto Beth-barah and Jordan."

question: Which two Midianite princes were captured and slain, and what historical names were given to the sites of their execution?

explanation: Oreb ('Raven') was executed at the Rock of Oreb, and Zeeb ('Wolf') was slain at the Winepress of Zeeb, celebrated in Psalm 83:11 and Isaiah 10:26 as a monumental day of divine deliverance. Judges 7:25 (KJV) - "And they took two princes of the Midianites, Oreb and Zeeb; and they slew Oreb upon the rock Oreb, and Zeeb they slew at the winepress of Zeeb, and pursued Midian, and brought the heads of Oreb and Zeeb to Gideon on the other side Jordan."

question: What sharp diplomatic complaint did the prideful men of Ephraim bring against Gideon?
opt1: Why hast thou plundered the gold of Midian without presenting tithes at Shiloh?

Judges 8:1 (KJV) - "And the men of Ephraim said unto him, Why hast thou served us thus, that thou calledst us not, when thou wentest to fight with the Midianites? And they did chide with him sharply."

question: What wise, humble answer did Gideon give that pacified the fierce anger of the Ephraimites?
opt1: Is not the gleaning of the grapes of Ephraim better than the vintage of Abi-ezr? God hath delivered into your hands the princes of Midian, Oreb and Zeeb

opt3: The high priest Eleazar commanded that only Manasseh should blow the trumpets
opt4: Draw your broadswords and let us settle this matter between the mountains
correct: Is not the gleaning of the grapes of Ephraim better than the vintage of Abi-ezr? God hath delivered into your hands the princes of Midian, Oreb and Zeeb
explanation: Illustrating Proverbs 15:1 ('A soft answer turneth away wrath'), Gideon humbly exalted Ephraim's capture of the two princes above his own clan's entire military campaign, averting civil war. Judges 8:2-3 (KJV) - "And he said unto them, What have I done now in comparison of you? Is not the gleaning of the grapes of Ephraim better than the vintage of Abi-ezer?... Then their anger was abated toward him, when he had said that."

question: How did Scripture describe the physical condition of Gideon and his three hundred warriors as they crossed Jordan?
opt1: Exultant and riding upon royal horses

opt4: Resting quietly in the shade of the terebinths

Judges 8:4 (KJV) - "And Gideon came to Jordan, and passed over, he, and the three hundred men that were with him, faint, yet pursuing them."

question: Why did the princes of Succoth and the men of Penuel refuse to give bread to Gideon's exhausted warriors?
opt1: Because an acute drought had depleted all the grain storage in their cities

opt3: Are the hands of Zebah and Zalmunna now in thine hand, that we should give bread unto thine army?

correct: Are the hands of Zebah and Zalmunna now in thine hand, that we should give bread unto thine army?
explanation: Cowardly and cynical, Succoth and Penuel refused to help their brethren until they saw whether Gideon could actually defeat the two Midianite kings with only 300 men. Judges 8:6, 8 (KJV) - "And the princes of Succoth said, Are the hands of Zebah and Zalmunna now in thine hand, that we should give bread unto thine army?"

question: What punishment did Gideon promise and execute upon the seventy-seven elders of Succoth upon his return?

explanation: Gideon exacted severe, memorable discipline: using rugged desert thorns and briers, he scourged the unfaithful elders of Succoth for betraying God's warriors. Judges 8:7, 16 (KJV) - "And he took the elders of the city, and thorns of the wilderness and briers, and with them he taught the men of Succoth."

question: What did Gideon do to the defiant fortified city of Penuel?
opt1: He beat down the tower of Penuel, and slew the men of the city

opt4: He demanded forty talents of silver as annual tribute from their merchants

explanation: Penuel boasted in their high defensive watchtower; Gideon demolished their prideful tower and executed the treacherous leaders who refused bread to God's army. Judges 8:17 (KJV) - "And he beat down the tower of Penuel, and slew the men of the city."

question: Who were the two supreme kings of Midian whom Gideon personally executed at Karkor?
opt1: Oreb and Zeeb, princes of the desert

opt4: Eglon and Balak, sovereigns of Moab

explanation: Zebah ('Sacrifice') and Zalmunna ('Deprived of Protection') had murdered Gideon's brothers at Mount Tabor; Gideon executed them and took the crescent ornaments from their camels. Judges 8:12, 21 (KJV) - "...Then Zebah and Zalmunna said, Rise thou, and fall upon us: for as the man is, so is his strength. And Gideon arose, and slew Zebah and Zalmunna, and took away the ornaments that were on their camels' necks."

question: What noble theological declaration did Gideon proclaim when the men of Israel asked him to establish a hereditary royal dynasty?
opt1: I shall rule over you until my hair is grey, and then appoint the high priest
opt2: The tribe of Judah alone hath the divine right to provide a king over the land

opt4: Let the seventy elders assemble at Shiloh to crown me with a circlet of gold
correct: I will not rule over you, neither shall my son rule over you: the LORD shall rule over you
explanation: Gideon correctly recognized Israel as a theocracy: God alone was their King, and no mortal man should usurp God's supreme sovereign throne over His covenant people. Judges 8:22-23 (KJV) - "Then the men of Israel said unto Gideon, Rule thou over us, both thou, and thy son, and thy son's son also: for thou hast delivered us from the hand of Midian. And Gideon said unto them, I will not rule over you, neither shall my son rule over you: the LORD shall rule over you."

question: What tragic spiritual compromise did Gideon commit with the 1,700 shekels of golden earrings collected from the prey?
opt1: He cast a golden calf like Aaron and placed it upon Mount Gerizim

opt3: He built a private royal palace of cedar wood rivaling the tabernacle

explanation: Despite his earlier humility, Gideon fashioned a lavish priestly vestment (ephod) in his hometown, establishing an unauthorized rival religious shrine that led his household and the nation into spiritual idolatry. Judges 8:26-27 (KJV).

question: What did the children of Israel do as soon as Gideon died in a good old age?
opt1: Turned again, and went a whoring after Baalim, and made Baal-berith their god, and remembered not the LORD their God

explanation: No sooner had Gideon died than the fickle nation relapsed into paganism, making 'Baal-berith' ('Lord of the Covenant') their idol and showing no loyalty to Gideon's family. Judges 8:33-35 (KJV) - "And it came to pass, as soon as Gideon was dead, that the children of Israel turned again, and went a whoring after Baalim, and made Baal-berith their god. And the children of Israel remembered not the LORD their God, who had delivered them out of the hands of all their enemies on every side:"

question: Who was the ruthless son of Gideon by his Shechemite concubine who conspired to seize the kingship?
opt1: Abimelech the son of Jerubbaal (Gideon)
opt2: Jotham the youngest son who hid in the cave
opt3: Phinehas the son of Eleazar the priest
opt4: Gaal the son of Ebed the Canaanite rebel
correct: Abimelech the son of Jerubbaal (Gideon)
explanation: Abimelech ('My father is king' - an ironic name) appealed to tribal nepotism among his mother's relatives in Shechem to launch a bloody coup against his brothers. Judges 9:1-2 (KJV) - "And Abimelech the son of Jerubbaal went to Shechem unto his mother's brethren, and communed with them... Whether is better for you, either that all the sons of Jerubbaal, which are threescore and ten persons, reign over you, or that one reign over you? remember also that I am your bone and your flesh."

question: With what blood money provided from the temple of Baal-berith did Abimelech finance his murderous coup?
opt1: Forty talents of refined gold plundered from the city of Thebez

opt3: One hundred talents of silver extracted as taxes from Mount Ephraim
opt4: Fifty golden crescents taken from the camels of the kings of Midian
correct: Threescore and ten pieces of silver out of the house of Baal-berith, wherewith Abimelech hired vain and light persons
explanation: The idolatrous temple of Baal-berith financed the slaughter: with seventy pieces of silver, Abimelech hired ruthless mercenaries to assassinate Gideon's seventy sons. Judges 9:4 (KJV) - "And they gave him threescore and ten pieces of silver out of the house of Baal-berith, wherewith Abimelech hired vain and light persons, which followed him."

question: Where did Abimelech murder his brothers, and which solitary brother survived by hiding himself?

opt3: Slew his brethren the sons of Jerubbaal, being threescore and ten persons, upon one stone at Ophrah: notwithstanding yet Jotham the youngest son was left; for he hid himself

correct: Slew his brethren the sons of Jerubbaal, being threescore and ten persons, upon one stone at Ophrah: notwithstanding yet Jotham the youngest son was left; for he hid himself
explanation: In cold-blooded execution, Abimelech butchered his brothers on a single execution stone at Ophrah, but the youngest boy, Jotham, successfully hid and escaped. Judges 9:5 (KJV) - "And he went unto his father's house at Ophrah, and slew his brethren the sons of Jerubbaal, being threescore and ten persons, upon one stone: notwithstanding yet Jotham the youngest son of Jerubbaal was left; for he hid himself."

question: From the summit of which mount did Jotham proclaim his famous prophetic fable of the trees?
opt1: From the peak of Mount Ebal beside the plastered altar

correct: He went and stood in the top of mount Gerizim, and lifted up his voice, and cried
explanation: Gerizim was the traditional mount of blessing (Deut 27:12); from its towering crags Jotham shouted down his satirical parable warning Shechem of their folly. Judges 9:7 (KJV) - "And when they told it to Jotham, he went and stood in the top of mount Gerizim, and lifted up his voice, and cried, and said unto them, Hearken unto me, ye men of Shechem, that God may hearken unto you."

question: Which three noble, productive trees refused the invitation to reign over the trees in Jotham's parable?
opt1: The olive tree, the fig tree, and the vine
opt2: The cedar of Lebanon, the tall oak of Bashan, and the green fir tree

opt4: The weeping willow of Jordan, the desert acacia, and the myrtle tree

explanation: The productive plants refused to leave their God-given callings (olive fatness, fig sweetness, wine that cheers God and man) to wave fruitlessly over other trees, representing worthy men refusing selfish tyranny. Judges 9:8-13 (KJV).

question: Which worthless, dangerous plant accepted the crown and threatened to devour the cedars of Lebanon with fire?
opt1: The wild thistle that grew along the stony paths of Samaria

opt3: The poisonous hemlock that blossomed in the furrows of the field
opt4: The desert weed that dried up under the burning east wind

explanation: The bramble (symbolizing worthless Abimelech) could offer no real shade, only prickly thorns and combustible kindling that would inevitably ignite and destroy the magnificent cedars. Judges 9:14-15 (KJV) - "Then said all the trees unto the bramble, Come thou, and reign over us. And the bramble said unto the trees, If in truth ye anoint me king over you, then come and put your trust in my shadow: and if not, let fire come out of the bramble, and devour the cedars of Lebanon."

question: How long did Abimelech reign over Israel before God sent an evil spirit of discord between him and Shechem?

opt4: Forty years, throughout a generation of unbroken peace

explanation: Abimelech's illicit, blood-soaked regime lasted only three years before divine justice intervened, turning his co-conspirators against him in mutual hatred. Judges 9:22-23 (KJV) - "When Abimelech had reigned three years over Israel, Then God sent an evil spirit between Abimelech and the men of Shechem; and the men of Shechem dealt treacherously with Abimelech:"

question: What did Abimelech do to the city of Shechem after conquering it and slaughtering its inhabitants?

explanation: Sowing a captured city with salt was an ancient symbolic act denoting total obliteration and perpetual barrenness, ensuring it could yield no life. Judges 9:45 (KJV) - "And Abimelech fought against the city all that day; and he took the city, and slew the people that was therein, and beat down the city, and sowed it with salt."

question: How did Abimelech incinerate the one thousand men and women sheltering in the hold of the temple of the god Berith?

opt3: He launched burning jars of pitch from catapults positioned upon Mount Ebal
opt4: He starved them through a forty-day siege until their cisterns ran dry

explanation: Fulfilling Jotham's prophetic curse that fire would come out from the bramble, Abimelech burned the tower with branches from Mount Zalmon, cremating one thousand citizens alive. Judges 9:48-49 (KJV) - "...so that all the men of the tower of Shechem died also, about a thousand men and women."

opt2: And a certain woman cast a piece of a millstone upon Abimelech's head, and all to brake his skull

opt4: A champion of Thebez challenged him to single combat and pierced his heart

explanation: Poetic divine justice: the tyrant who murdered his seventy brothers on a single stone had his own skull crushed by an upper millstone dropped by a woman from the tower wall. Judges 9:53 (KJV) - "And a certain woman cast a piece of a millstone upon Abimelech's head, and all to brake his skull."

question: Who was the judge from the tribe of Issachar that defended Israel for twenty-three years and dwelt in Shamir?

opt4: Abdon the son of Hillel the Pirathonite

Judges 10:1-2 (KJV) - "And after Abimelech there arose to defend Israel Tola the son of Puah, the son of Dodo, a man of Issachar; and he dwelt in Shamir in mount Ephraim. And he judged Israel twenty and three years, and died, and was buried in Shamir."

question: What notable detail is recorded concerning the family and possessions of Jair the Gileadite?

Judges 10:3-4 (KJV) - "And after him arose Jair, a Gileadite, and judged Israel twenty and two years. And he had thirty sons that rode on thirty ass colts, and they had thirty cities, which are called Havoth-jair unto this day, which are in the land of Gilead."

question: How many foreign national pantheons did apostate Israel serve according to the catalogue in Judges 10:6?

opt4: Seven false god cults: Baalim, Ashtaroth, and the gods of Syria, Zidon, Moab, Ammon, and the Philistines

explanation: Israel reached a nadir of spiritual promiscuity, incorporating the idols of every surrounding pagan culture—Syria, Phoenicia, Moab, Ammon, and Philistia. Judges 10:6 (KJV) - "And the children of Israel did evil again in the sight of the LORD, and served Baalim, and Ashtaroth, and the gods of Syria, and the gods of Zidon, and the gods of Moab, and the gods of the children of Ammon, and the gods of the Philistines, and forsook the LORD, and served not him."

question: For how many years did the Ammonites and Philistines severely crush and oppress Israel east and west of Jordan?

question: How many past historical oppressions did the LORD recount to Israel when they initially cried out for help in Judges 10:11-12?

question: What piercing, sarcastic rebuke did God give to the crying Israelites before they genuinely repented?
opt1: Pay seventy talents of silver into the treasury of the tabernacle

question: What two essential actions demonstrated Israel's genuine inward repentance in Judges 10:15-16?
opt1: They offered forty unblemished heifers and tore down the walls of Gilgal

explanation: True biblical repentance involves both verbal confession of unworthiness and active radical removal of idolatrous objects from the community. Judges 10:15-16 (KJV).

question: How did God respond emotionally when Israel put away their idols and returned to Him?
opt1: And his soul was grieved for the misery of Israel

opt4: And he sent an angel of destruction to smite their firstborn cattle

explanation: A profound revelation of God's compassionate heart: though His holiness judged their sin, His fatherly heart could not bear to see His repentant people in misery. Judges 10:16 (KJV) - "And they put away the strange gods from among them, and served the LORD: and his soul was grieved for the misery of Israel."

question: Where did the children of Israel assemble and encamp to confront the invading Ammonite army?

Judges 10:17 (KJV) - "Then the children of Ammon were gathered together, and encamped in Gilead. And the children of Israel assembled themselves together, and encamped in Mizpeh."

question: What promise was proclaimed by the elders of Gilead to anyone who would lead the battle against Ammon?

opt4: He shall be exempted from all tribal taxes throughout his lifetime

Judges 10:18 (KJV) - "And the people and princes of Gilead said one to another, What man is he that will begin to fight against the children of Ammon? he shall be head over all the inhabitants of Gilead."

question: Why had Jephthah the Gileadite been cast out from his father's house by his legitimate brothers?

opt4: Because he had conspired to surrender the pastures of Tob to Ammon
